paragraphs: The Samaritans do not acknowledge any prophet other than "Moses" and "Joshua," and do not believe in anything of the books of prophecy except the Torah and the book of "Joshua." They do not recognize the Temple, and their prayer is toward Shechem. To this day they offer the sacrifices, and they have a priest who does not mix with them and does not take wives from among them — so far as has reached us. They do not mix with others nor draw near to anyone; and if one not of them drew near them, they washed themselves of him.

It is reported of them that they take the heads of the months by an intercalation of their own, which they call the intercalation of "Jeroboam." It is also reported of them that if a garment became impure for them, they put it in a jar-like vessel or the like, stopped up the vessel's mouth, and put it into water — and the garment, with them, was thereby purified without touching the water; for in this they took the saying of Scripture [Lev 11:32]: "וּבָא בַמַּיִם."
They are two groups: one of them called "Kūshān," the other "Dustān." One of the two groups does not acknowledge the maʿād (the world to come).

They have altered things in the reading of the Torah — of this, that they read [Exod 20:18]: "וְכָל הָעָם שׁוֹמְעִים אֶת הַקֹּלֹת" (for "רֹאִים"); and that they read [Gen 4:8]: "וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו: קוּם נֵצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה" (an addition to the Masoretic text); and other things, some of which will appear in our account of the doctrine of "Ismaʿīl al-ʿUkbarī."
: Shechem — Mount Gerizim — is the Samaritan sanctuary, toward which their prayer is directed.
: A pointed identification, linking the Samaritan calendar to the Jeroboamite calendar described in bab 2, §1 — part of Q's historiographical thesis. Cf. Erder, Mourners of Zion, ch. 2.
: The two groups "Kūshān" and "Dustān," Samaritan sub-sects; the identifications are uncertain in modern scholarship.
: A noteworthy notice on the Samaritans and the afterlife.
: The Samaritan reading "שׁוֹמְעִים" ("hearing") for "רֹאִים" ("seeing") — the Samaritan qere.
: The Samaritan addition at Gen 4:8, paralleled in the Qumran text and part of the Septuagint tradition.
